subject: Over or underestimation of sedentary behavior

messages.author: f8d803b4db325843
messages.subject: Over or underestimation of sedentary behavior
parts:
Dear Vincent,

I am working with GGIR to analyze 24-hour movement behaviors retrieved from Actigraph GT3X data (7 days, 100 Hz). For each included participant I make a report with individual details on their behaviors. However, I noticed some conflicting results when interpreting output of GGIR and the profile of the participant. I added two examples underneath the script. I was wondering if there is a explanation for the conflicting results?

g.shell.GGIR(

  #=====================

  # Part 1

  #=====================

  mode=c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),

  datadir="C:/Users/irwillem/GGIR/Data_OwOb_GT3X",

  outputdir="C:/Users/irwillem/GGIR/Output",

  overwrite = TRUE,

  do.parallel = TRUE,

  idloc = 6,

  do.report=c(2, 4, 5),

 

  #=====================

  # Part 2

  #=====================

  strategy = 1,

  hrs.del.start = 24,          hrs.del.end = 0,

  includedaycrit = 16,

  qwindow=c(0,24),

  mvpathreshold =c(69),

  bout.metric = 6,

  includenightcrit = 16,

  dofirstpage = TRUE,

 

  # Part 3 + 4

  #=====================

  timethreshold= c(5),

  anglethreshold=5,

  ignorenonwear = TRUE,

  excludefirst.part4 = TRUE,

  def.noc.sleep = 1,

  outliers.only = TRUE,

  criterror = 4,

  do.visual = TRUE,

 

  # Part 5 #

  #=====================

  threshold.lig=c(30), threshold.mod=c(69), threshold.vig=c(260),

  boutcriter.in = 0.9, boutcriter.lig = 0.9, boutcriter.mvpa = 0.9,

  boutdur.in = c(30), boutdur.lig = c(30), boutdur.mvpa = c(1, 10, 30),

  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

  timewindow = c("WW"),

  dayborder = 3,

  visualreport=TRUE,

  week_weekend_aggregate.part5 = TRUE,

  frag.metrics = "all",

  part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE

)

 

Example 1

When running the GGIR script for participant X, I got these results with rather low PA (LPA en MPA) levels and high sedentary behavior levels. However this participant is a nurse where it is expected that she performs more LPA. I asked this participant for more feedback on her week and she stated that she had a rather active week with a lot of walking activity during her working hours.

Therefore, I think that these results give rather an OVERestimation of SB. Next, I uploaded the data in Actilife to explore her results. The blue lines indicate activity intensities where this graph shows rather active days. (period marked in red is the sleeping period)


 

 

Example 2

Participant Y has a rather active behavior profile with rather small sedentary behavior levels (only 96 minutes a day) when interpreting the output in GGIR. However, this person has a sedentary job where he sits a lot during the working hours. This person questions his GGIR results as sedentary behavior could represents an UNDERestimation. 


As I explore his file in Actilife, I got the following result. The blue lines indicate that he has some active periods but also longer periods of sedentary behavior. This is inconsistent with the  results out of GGIR.



Thanks in advance for your time.

Kind regards,

Iris Willems

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Over or underestimation of sedentary behavior
parts:
Dear Iris,

I see you chose a moderate threshold of 69 with a 1 minute epoch without considering consider bouts. The possible explanations that may be worth investigating:
  • Threshold choice in relation to wear location and age group: I am guessing you are working with hip data, correct? If not, how did you arrive at this threshold? If yes, then I suppose what you do is in line with literature for adult populations https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/CutPoints.html
  • Calibration of the data: Should not be a problem if you have several days of data with good compliance. See part2_summary variable calib_err, if this is below 0.005 then it should be good.
  • Choice of metric in relation to wear location. Metric ENMO has primarily been motivated for studies with wrist-worn sensors. It may be worth trying out the MAD metric (see cut-points Vähä-Ypyä 2015).
  • Discrepancy with analytical approach by Actilife setting used. If you used Actilife to classify behaviour based on shorter epochs then I would expect that to result in more active time. If Actilife was used with some kind of bout or sojourn detection algorithm then I would expect it to result in lest active time.
  • Mix-up of participant IDs. Double check that start date makes sense and is consistent between Actilife and GGIR. Ideally we never make these kind of mistakes, but can be good to double check.

Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

parts:
Dear Vincent, 

Thank you for the response. I checked your suggestions above but did not find any mistakes. Additionally, I contacted this testperson and he is normally very sedentary as he sits a whole day at work. When I look at the visualization of this person, I see a lot of LPA which seems rather incorrect. Does this looks normal for you? I used the cut-off points of Hildebrand for hip worn Actigraphs.


Thanks in advance for your help,

Iris Willems

parts:
Dear Vincent,

A follow up on the previous mail. This is the visual for example 1. She is a nurse and walks all day so normally she would have a lot of LPA (which can be seen in raw data). Therefore it is strange that all her movement is categorized as inactivity. In the visual there is a note 'arm movement', where the participants wore the device on the hip. But I used the cut-off points of Hildebrand for hip worn actigraph so normally this should be correct? Do you have any idea what can be wrong?
Thank in advance for helping me.

parts:
Hi Iris,

Does the part 5 csv report also indicate the there is a lot of time spent in light PA?

If not, then this may be a bug in the code used for the visualisation which does its own simplified detections of intensity levels... We are aware of this and it on our wish list to improve this.

If yes, then maybe it truly is the data itself. Would it be possible for you to share with me the corresponding .RData file from the meta/basic folder for me to investigate further?

Thanks,

Vincent
